Q4. who collected the data

The May 2021 National Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates for the United States were collected by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).


Q5. When was the data collected? What time period does it cover? 

The May 2021 National Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates for the United States was released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) on March 31, 2022. The data reflects employment and wage estimates for May 2021.

Q7. What is the scope of the data? For example, what set of people, hospitals, or insurance plans does it cover? Is it complete data for the full population (e.g. all hospitals that accept Medicare), a sample (e.g. randomly selected survey respondents), summary measures for different groups or geographical areas (e.g. the value for each state), or something else?  

The May 2021 National Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates is a set of summary measures for different occupations across the United States. It covers the entire country and reports data on employment and wage estimates for over 800 occupations based on the Occupational Employment Statistics (OES) survey, which is conducted by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). The data is not comprehensive, as it is based on a sample of non-farm establishments that are selected to represent various industries and regions in the U.S.

Q9. Count the number of rows and columns. Are these numbers what you were expecting? 

```{r}
# Loading
library("readxl")
library(ggplot2)
library(psych)
library(magrittr)
library(dplyr) 
# xls files
NA_data <- read_excel("D:/Toqeer_work/April/Advance Data Modeling for Health Analytics/week 1/national_M2021_dl.xlsx", sheet = 1, na = c("", "N/A"))
num_rows <- nrow(NA_data)
num_cols <- ncol(NA_data)

# print the results
cat("Number of rows:", num_rows, "\n")
cat("Number of columns:", num_cols, "\n")

#.
```
